GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2014-03-07T14:51:55Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Control over PUT vs POST for models with supplied IDs
Description: ``` javascript

var UserModel = Backbone.Model.extend({
    idAttribute: "username",
    urlRoot: "/userapi"
});

var newUser = new UserModel();
newUser.set('username','v0idnull');
newUser.save();
```

I can not create a new user with this code.

Backbone makes the assumption that whatever API you are calling, the unique identifier for resource you're manipulating is generated on creation. But this is not always the case. In this above example, the unique identifier is the username, and so the ID is provided.

But that code will always try to do a PUT request on /userapi/v0idnull and it will always fail with a 404.

I think there are many different ways of solving this, from providing create() and update() methods on the model (that save() can use), to changing

``` javascript
method = this.isNew() ? 'create' : (options.patch ? 'patch' : 'update');
```

to exposing the method through the options hash of the save() method:

``` javascript
method = options.method ? options.method : (this.isNew() ? 'create' : (options.patch ? 'patch' : 'update');
```

With a change like this, I can do one of two things:

My application is aware of when I'm creating a user and when I'm updating a user and call the appropriate method / set the appropriate option

OR

I call save normally which tries a PUT, gets a 404, and an error handler tries save again, forcing a POST.

Thoughts?
